Q1: Which operator-step holds should be refused and escalated instead?
Choices:
- A: All of them. Never write a `placeholder_retired` hold again. Every operator-step fix-up escalates once, and the hold kind is kept only so existing markers can still be read.
- B: Only steps that are not "set a repository variable or secret". Keep the hold when the verdict's `operator_instructions` say to set a repo Actions variable or secret with exactly that placeholder name. Escalate for any other kind of step, such as a workflow or path grant, pinning an action SHA, or a label repair, where nobody will ever create a variable with that name. (RECOMMENDED)
- C: Only steps where the verdict's `operator_instructions` name a different variable or secret from the placeholder. Hold on the real name they give instead, and escalate only when no real name can be found.
Q2: What should "escalate the item once" do?
Choices:
- A: Post one comment on the item quoting the verdict's `operator_instructions` (the real action needed), add a marker so it is never posted again, and stop judging the item until a person posts its resume command. The `ai:operator-step` issue entry that the verdict already writes stays as it is. (RECOMMENDED)
- B: Do everything in A, and also send a Telegram alert.
- C: Do everything in A, and also add the existing human-attention or blocked label to the item (and to its fix-up, e.g. #178).
Q3: How should holds that are already open (mongo-explorer#51, radateeree-resort.com#174) be handled?
Choices:
- A: Change only new holds. The existing ones expire under the 14-day default: #51 around 2026-11-15 and #174 around 2026-11-18. When the judge decides again after expiry, it takes the new escalation path. (RECOMMENDED)
- B: Also check open `placeholder_retired` holds on the next run, and escalate and close any that match the Q1 rule straight away.
